title: Temporal KV Slot Decay and Adaptive Partitioning for Long-Context Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a temporal decay + adaptive partitioning algorithm for KV cache slot residency tailored to Llama, Mistral, and Qwen long-context variants. The feature creates model-specific decay constants and assigns KV slots to hot/warm/cold partitions with a lightweight 'lease' mechanism to avoid thrashing during bursty traffic and continuous batching windows. Goals: reduce peak GPU memory pressure, lower OOM incidence for 64k+ token workloads, and improve tail latency stability under mixed batch sizes.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model decay profile exists for Llama-2-Chat, Mistral-7B, Qwen-7B and can be toggled via model config
KV slot residency is partitioned into hot/warm/cold and visible in the runtime memory dashboard
End-to-end integration passes perf regression suite: no >2% increase in median latency for short requests, tail latency (p95/p99) reduced by >=10% under sustained long-context load
Observed reduction in peak VRAM usage by >=12% on A100-80GB for 128k context synthetic workload
Feature gated behind runtime-1.20 feature flag and rolloutable per-customer
Automated tests covering eviction score calc, lease renewal, and partition rebalancing
comments: 2026-02-16 - Kickoff: Spiked a prototype that computes an eviction score = alpha * time_since_last_access + beta * recency_weight + gamma * batch_hotness. Using alpha tuned per model improves long-context residency decisions compared to simple LRU.

2026-02-20 - Bench v1: Synthetic 64k token chat stream across 8 concurrent sessions showed 18% reduction in VRAM high-water mark but 4% CPU overhead on the host for eviction bookkeeping. Data: https://datadog.redwood.com/dashboards/kv-decay (internal)

2026-02-26 - Design decision: implement a 3-tier partition (hot/warm/cold) with deterministic promotion/demotion rules to make memory compaction and slab reclaiming predictable. Avoided micro-churn approach due to eviction jitter observed in early experiments.

2026-03-01 - Review feedback from @Diego Ramirez: request to add quantization-awareness to eviction score (prefer evict slots used by quantized weights last) and to include tenant isolation heuristics for Dedicated pools.

2026-03-03 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4210. Contains eviction score implementation, lease mechanism, and metrics emission (slot_age, slot_partition, eviction_reason).

2026-03-04 - Perf run on H100-80GB: 11% tail latency improvement p99 under mixed batching with continuous batching enabled. Noted a 1.8% increase in median latency for <64 token requests; trade-off acceptable for enterprise long-context customers.

2026-03-05 - Blocker discovered: on multi-variant GPUs with heavy shared workloads, warm->cold demotions plus compaction induced short GC spikes. Mitigation: stagger compaction windows and add cost-based throttling. Follow-up ticket planned.
NEXT STEPS: finalize model-specific alpha/beta/gamma lookup table, add quantization-aware signal, integrate with autoscaler routing policies, and roll out to runtime-1.20 canary group.
